From: Sara Leconte <sara.leconte@globalhealthit.eu>

Cc: DPO - GlobalHealth IT <dpo@globalhealthit.eu>; Procurement <procurement@globalhealthit.eu>
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: EU-only processing attestation & subprocessor export-control evidence

Hi Vanessa,

Following up on our procurement checklist for the platform evaluation (RFP GHIT-2028-145). Our legal and DPO teams require:  

- A signed attestation stating Redwood will only process GHIT customer data within the EU (data plane, backups, and disaster recovery replicas).
- A current subprocessor roster and confirmation that any subprocessors with potential non-EU access are either restricted or covered by SCCs and additional contractual controls.
- Details on the KMS key locations used to protect customer data (are keys EU-resident and customer-dedicated?).
- Confirmation about jurisdictional access: do any Redwood employees in non-EU regions have administrative or emergency access to EU tenant data? If so, please list the controls (just-in-time access, audit trails, approvals).
- A network/dataflow diagram showing where data at rest, backups, and logs live (we need something we can attach to our Schrems II / SCCs review).

We are aiming to close procurement by 2028-10-20. Could you provide the attestation and the subprocessor CSV by 2028-10-12? If you need a template for the attestation, we can share one.

Thanks,

Sara Leconte
Procurement Manager
GlobalHealth IT

Key questions we need to confirm quickly:

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Oct 2028 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: EU-only processing attestation & subprocessor export-control evidence

Vanessa / Kimberly — thanks. Quick summary of what I'll produce and a few technical clarifications we should convey to GHIT in the attestation so it is defensible under Schrems II review:  

- Attestation draft: clear statement that for GHIT (tenant/account GHIT-2028-145) Redwood will route and store production data, backups, and DR replicas exclusively in EU regions listed in the attestation. We'll include a table of the AWS/GCP/Azure regions used for EU-only customers.
- Subprocessor roster: provide a CSV (attached) with each subprocessors' primary region, whether they hold access credentials, and whether they perform any out-of-band support. Flagged subprocessors that may require supplemental SCCs or additional contractual commitments will be annotated.
- KMS: we can offer two options in writing — (A) platform-managed EU-resident keys (we can confirm key material is stored in EU HSM-backed KMS clusters) or (B) customer-managed keys (BYOK) where the customer holds key control; we will include the operational tradeoffs.
- Administrative access: we cannot state that no Redwood employee outside the EU might ever gain emergency access (e.g., on-call escalation), but we will state that any cross-region admin access is governed by JIT access approval, MFA, auditable session logs, and that access requests are reviewed by Security and logged. We will attach our access-control summary and a redacted audit sample.

I will attach:
- subprocessor_list_20281010.csv (redacted where vendor NDA requires)
- redwood-eu-dataflow-20281011.drawio.png
- a one-page attestation PDF for signature (redwood-eu-only-attestation-GHIT-20281011.pdf)

I will also include a short paragraph mapping the attestation statements to the corresponding SCC clauses and the compensating technical measures (KMS residency, JIT access, logging, contractual SCCs). That should help GHIT's DPO connect the dots.

Kimberly — if you can confirm the list of regions we plan to reference and validate KMS residency, I will finalize and sign.

Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel — Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference
